product_description: Colourful handmade upcycled polythene weave rakhi with beads handcrafted for the very special khatta meetha bond between brother and sister.The Recycled Plastic project was launched in 2010. During its initial phase, Khamir trained 12 women to wash, cut and weave plastic collected from industrial and residential areas. After the pilot program proved successful, Khamir scaled the initiative to include more people in the production chain and develop more woven plastic products. The plastic collection is coordinated with the help of Sahjeevan, an environmental NGO based in Bhuj that also works on urban issues. Collected plastic is transported to Khamir, where it is cleaned and segregated on the basis of colour and quality. The clean plastic is cut into long strips, which are then given to weavers. The weaving is carried out both on traditional pit looms as well as frame looms. Plastic weaving is currently practiced by a large number of women trained by Khamir. During its initial phase, Khamir trained 12 women to wash, cut and weave plastic collected from industrial and residential areas. After the pilot program proved successful, Khamir scaled the initiative to include more people in the production chain and develop more woven plastic products. The plastic collection is coordinated with the help of Sahjeevan, an environmental NGO based in Bhuj that also works on urban issues. Collected plastic is transported to Khamir, where it is cleaned and segregated on the basis of colour and quality. The clean plastic is cut into long strips, which are then given to weavers. The weaving is carried out both on traditional pit looms as well as frame looms. Plastic weaving is currently practiced by a large number of women trained by Khamir. product_description:
Fine quality multicolor soof stitch embroidery pure handloom mashru silk sling flap bag. It has one zipper pocket inside & one zipper pocket on backside. Ample space to keep most of your essentials.
Soof Embroidery is probably the best kind of art amongst Gujarat's long-standing tradition of embroidery of distinct styles, and is characterised by vibrant colours and mirror work. Soof, meaning 'neat and clean'. The surface satin stitch is worked from the back of the fabric by counting the weave of the fabric and inserting the needle of regular and designed intervals. The designs for Soof embroidery cannot be pre drawn and are left to the discretion of the individual craftswomen, who need a good grasp of a geometry to work out their designs.

Srikalahasti handpainted kalamkari sling bag by Dwaraka Plus is crafted from cotton and features traditional tagai work. It has a spacious main compartment and an outer zipper pocket for easy access to essentials. Its sling strap makes it ideal for daily use, shopping, travel, and casual outings. Handpainted by skilled rural women artisans, it showcases traditional srikalahasti kalamkari, where designs are drawn using a kalam (bamboo pen) and filled with colours naturally derived from leaves, flowers, and plant sources. Dwaraka Plus, founded in 1998 by Anita Reddy and Dwaraknath Reddy, is a not for profit, artisan-owned initiative supporting artisans and preserving traditional kalamkari craftsmanship.
A Note on Handmade Beauty
Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges, or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage, and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature, because no two pieces are ever alike.

product_description:

This piece showcases the art of kalamkari, where each design is hand-drawn using a “kalam” (bamboo stick) and filled with natural colours. This jewellery box features three utility hooks, an elastic inner pocket, and six compartments, keeping your rings, earrings, chains and accessories neatly organised and protected.
A Note on Handmade Beauty:
Each piece is hand painted and using natural colors over a slow process of 30–35 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges, or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage, and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature because no two pieces are ever alike.

product_title: Brown - Handpainted Kalamkari Natural Dyed Ghicha Silk Clutch / Wallet 31

The clutch / wallet is designed for everyday use and features five pockets inside for better organization, making it easy to carry essentials like cash, cards or small personal items.

Made by skilled artisans using traditional techniques, the potli bag is an exquisite accessory that is perfect for adding a touch of ethnic charm to any outfit. The intricate embroidery showcases the rich cultural heritage of the Kala Raksha community, and the attention to detail is evident in every stitch.Rabari embroidery is unique to the nomadic Rabaris. Essential to Rabari embroidery is the use of mirrors in a variety of shapes. Rabaris outline patterns in chain stitch, then decorate them with a regular sequence of mirrors and accent stitches, in a regular sequence of colors. Rabaris also use decorative back stitching, called bakhiya.

In this community, women wear an embroidered Choliand jacket after their marriage. Their embroidery style is mainly referred to as Pakko (which is predominantly used) and also comprises other stitches such as Neran, Kharek, Kambhiri. Their patterns are similar to that of Meghwar. Other than the embroidery, they do patch-work and applique. The Rajputs, who are historically the protector-warriors, as a community are conservative. The women of these clans are not allowed to go outside their faliya (colony). Embroidery is the only livelihood option for women of this densely populated community and hence comprises a fairly large share of Qasab’s creations.

Soof Embroidery is probably the best kind of art amongst Gujarat's long-standing tradition of embroidery of distinct styles, and is characterised by vibrant colours and mirror work. product_title: Rajasthani Men Handmade Puppet/Kathputli
product_description: Beautifully handcrafted Rajasthani dancing men puppet / kathputli. In Rajasthan the puppet tradition is called Kathputli, where Kaath means wood and Putli means Puppet. Kathputli means a puppet made out of wood. However Kathputlis typically have wooden torso and shoulders while the legs (absent in the ones based on a female character) and arms are made of clothes stuffed with cotton. Kathputli’s are string puppets controlled by strings which passes from the top of the puppets and manipulated by the puppeteer. These highly decorative handmade puppets are the source of age old tradition of narration of historical stories, myths and legends. The narrations were accompanied with music and dialogues delivered by the group members. Kathputli became one of the most important and well know performing arts of Rajasthan and it represents the tradition, customs and socio-cultural backdrop of the state.

product_description: Beautifully handcrafted Rajasthani dancing couple puppet / kathputli (small). In Rajasthan the puppet tradition is called Kathputli, where Kaath means wood and Putli means Puppet. Kathputli means a puppet made out of wood. However Kathputlis typically have wooden torso and shoulders while the legs (absent in the ones based on a female character) and arms are made of clothes stuffed with cotton. Kathputli’s are string puppets controlled by strings which passes from the top of the puppets and manipulated by the puppeteer. These highly decorative handmade puppets are the source of age old tradition of narration of historical stories, myths and legends. The narrations were accompanied with music and dialogues delivered by the group members. Kathputli became one of the most important and well know performing arts of Rajasthan and it represents the tradition, customs and socio-cultural backdrop of the state.

product_description:
Handcrafted Kondapalli wooden toy hand-painted with natural colours from Andhra Pradesh. Good play item for kids and nice for gifting or house decoration.

These toys were one of the variety of toys assembled in the houses during the festivals of Sankranti and Navratri and is referred as Bommala Koluvu.The art of crafting is a 400 year old tradition. The artisans who make the toys are referred as Aryakhastriyas (also known as Nakarshalu), who have their mention in the Brahmanda Purana.
The Kondapalli toys are made from soft wood known as Tella Poniki which are found in nearby Kondapalli Hills. Each part is carved out separately. Then makku- a paste of tamarind seed powder & sawdust is used to join pieces together, add details and finish the toys. The later step involves coloring with either oil and water-colours or vegetable dyes and enamel paints are applied based on the type of the toys. The artisans mainly work on producing figures of mythology, animals, birds, bullock carts, rural life etc., and the most notable one is Dasavataram, dancing dolls etc.

Beige natural dyed hand block print ajrakh cotton hakoba fabric made by master artisans of Kutch, Gujarat. It showcases the rich textile heritage of the region, where artisans continue a craft believed to be over 4,500 years old. It is created using delicate cutwork embroidery with intricate ajrakh hand block printing using natural dyes and the traditional resist-printing process. The Ajrakh artisans in India originally migrated from Sindh to the Kutch region of Gujarat and to Barmer in Rajasthan. Ajrakh is also the traditional attire of the Maldhari pastoral and Khatri communities of Bhuj, Gujarat. Made from pure cotton, it offers lasting comfort, ideal for creating elegant kurtas, shirts, dresses, dupattas or thoughtfully designed home décor items.
A Note on Handmade Beauty
Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage, and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature, because no two pieces are ever alike.

product_title: Brown - Kutch Organic Kala Cotton Mirror Work Pure Handwoven Fabric 09
product_description:
Brown kutch organic kala cotton mirror work fabric is handwoven by master artisan Vinay Siju from Bhuj, Gujarat, using the traditional kala cotton weaving practices of Kutch. Kala Cotton is one of India’s oldest indigenous cotton varieties, valued for its distinctive texture and deep connection to the region’s weaving traditions. The fabric is woven from organic cotton yarns and coloured using azo-free dyes. It offers a breathable texture, durable construction and a versatile drape, making it suitable for a variety of creations such as kurtas, shirts, dresses, jackets, stoles, bags and home decor accents.
Note : This piece carries tiny knots, thread pulls or uneven lines not flaws but fingerprints. Every irregularity is a whisper from the hands that made it. It’s what happens when tradition weaves through time not machines. If you’re looking for perfection, this isn’t it. But if you’re looking for soul you’ve found it.

product_title: Blue - Hand Block Batik Print Cotton Fabric 21
product_description:
Blue hand block batik print cotton fabric is crafted by master artisan Mohammed Sharif from Bherugarh, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, using the traditional wax-resist block printing process. Bherugarh, on the banks of river Shipra near Ujjain, became a hub of batik printing when craftsmen from Gujarat and Rajasthan settled here during the Mughal period, around 400 years ago. Heated wax is applied with intricately carved wooden blocks before dyeing, resisting colour to form delicate vein-like and webbed patterns unique to batik. Repeated waxing, dyeing and washing build layered motifs and rich depth. Ideal for ethnic wear, casual outfits or decor projects.
A Note on Handmade Beauty
Each piece is hand block printed and carefully dyed over a slow process of 15–20 days. product_title: Green - Ajrakh Vanaspati Hand Block Print Natural Dyed Cotton Fabric 14
product_description:
Green ajrakh vanaspati hand block print natural dyed cotton fabric is created using the traditional Ajrakh craft practiced for generations in the Barmer region of Rajasthan. Made through a meticulous process of hand block printing and natural dyeing, this fabric showcases the Vanaspati design, featuring floral and foliage-inspired motifs. Believed to be over 4,500 years old, Ajrakh is celebrated for its earthy colours, intricate detailing and layered printing techniques. The process involves multiple stages of resist printing, dyeing, washing and drying, with each colour applied only after a resting period, making every piece unique. Suitable for creating kurtas, shirts, dresses, tunics, co-ord sets, skirts, dupattas and home decor accents.
A Note on Handmade Beauty
Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color mild pigment smudges or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature because no two pieces are ever alike.

product_title: Pedana Hand Block Print Natural Dyed Kota Doria Cotton Kalamkari Fabric 08
product_description:
Kalamkari hand block print natural dyed kota doria cotton fabric from Pedana, Andhra Pradesh, showcases one of India’s oldest and most intricate textile printing traditions. Crafted by skilled master artisan Venkata Bhanu, the fabric is created using hand-carved wooden blocks and natural dyes, resulting in beautifully detailed Kalamkari motifs inspired by nature and traditional storytelling. Kota doria is an age-old Indian textile produced in the Kota district of Rajasthan. The Doria or the threads, are finely interwoven to create the characteristic check patterns. Its lightweight and sheer texture gives it an exquisite grace and elegance of its own. Ideal for creating kurtas, dresses, dupattas, saree blouses, and a variety of home decor accents, this fabric combines traditional artistry with versatile usability. Venkata Bhanu is a master artisan dedicated to preserving traditional Pedana Kalamkari using natural dyes and original techniques.
A Note on Handmade Beauty :
Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage, and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature because no two pieces are ever alike.

product_title: Brown - Ajrakh Hand Block Print Natural Dyed Handspun Handwoven Mulberry Silk Fabric 20
product_description:
Brown ajrakh hand block print natural dyed handspun handwoven mulberry silk fabric by master artisan Sufiyan Ismail Khatri from Kutch, crafted using traditional natural dyeing and resist block-printing techniques. This ancient craft is believed to be over 4,500 years old. The Ajrakh artisan community in India originally migrated from Sindh and later settled in the Kutch region of Gujarat and Barmer in Rajasthan. Ajrakh is also traditionally worn by the Maldhari pastoral community of Bhuj. The process is intricate and time-consuming, involving multiple stages of washing, dyeing, printing, and drying. Each layer of colour is carefully hand-printed only after a resting period, allowing the fabric to absorb the natural dyes completely. The rich texture of handspun, handwoven mulberry silk makes this fabric ideal for creating kurtas, shirts, dresses, dupattas, and even elegant home decor items.

product_title: Ajrakh Hand Block Print Merino Wool Handloom Natural Dyed Fabric 10
product_description:
Ajrakh hand block print merino wool handloom fabric is crafted in Kutch, Gujarat, using traditional resist block printing and natural dyeing techniques. Believed to be over 4,500 years old, this ancient craft traces its roots to artisans who migrated from Sindh to Kutch in Gujarat and Barmer in Rajasthan. Ajrakh is closely associated with the Maldhari pastoral & khatri community of Bhuj and is known for its intricate and time-intensive process, involving multiple stages of printing, dyeing and natural colour absorption. This fabric is ideal for winter wear, jackets, shawls, stoles and cozy apparel.
A Note on Handmade Beauty
Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges, or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage, and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature, because no two pieces are ever alike.

Ajrakh hand block print merino wool handloom fabric is crafted in Kutch, Gujarat, using traditional resist block printing and natural dyeing techniques. Believed to be over 4,500 years old, this ancient craft traces its roots to artisans who migrated from Sindh to Kutch in Gujarat and Barmer in Rajasthan. Ajrakh is closely associated with the Maldhari pastoral & khatri community of Bhuj and is known for its intricate and time-intensive process, involving multiple stages of printing, dyeing and natural colour absorption. This fabric is ideal for winter wear, jackets, shawls, stoles and cozy apparel.
A Note on Handmade Beauty
Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges, or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage, and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature, because no two pieces are ever alike.

product_title: Green - Authentic Kutch Hand Block Batik Print Pure Handwoven Natural Dyed Kala Cotton Fabric 70
product_description:
Authentic green hand block batik print pure handwoven natural dyed kala cotton fabric by Khamir, Kutch celebrates the centuries old batik tradition of Kutch, believed to have travelled to the region during the Ramayana era through skilled master craftsmen. Practised by the Khatri community, Batik became an important textile art of Kutch and was widely exported from Mandvi port to Indonesia since the 1500s. This fabric is created using the traditional wax-resist block printing technique, where heated wax is applied with intricately carved wooden blocks before dyeing. The wax resists colour, forming delicate vein-like and webbed patterns unique to batik. Repeated waxing, dyeing and washing create layered motifs and rich depth, making the fabric suitable for ethnic wear, contemporary outfits and home decor creations.
A Note on Handmade Beauty
Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges, or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. product_title: Blue - Exclusive! Pure Handspun Handwoven Pochampally Ikat Silk x Wool Fabric 15

Exclusive pure handspun handwoven blue pochampally ikat silk x wool fabric from Telangana, woven by skilled master artisans Shankar Gajam Govardhan. Pochampally, a small town in Telangana surrounded by lush green hills, is known for its rich handloom weaving traditions and distinctive Ikat textiles. Ikat is an ancient resist-dyeing technique where sections of yarn are carefully tied before being dyed with reactive dyes to create intricate patterns. These precisely tied and dyed yarns are then woven together in calculated alignment, forming beautifully detailed motifs on the fabric. product_title: Blue - Bagru Indigo Hand Block Print Kota Doria Natural Dyed Cotton Fabric 03
product_description:
Blue bagru indigo hand block print kota doria natural dyed cotton fabric comes from the village of Bagru in Rajasthan, where artisans have practiced the mud-resist printing technique for over 400–450 years. The fabric is created by applying a hand-prepared mud resist using carved wooden blocks, followed by dyeing with natural colours. After dyeing, the resist is washed away to reveal distinct patterns. Kota doria is an age-old Indian textile produced in the Kota district of Rajasthan. The fine threads are intricately interwoven to create its characteristic check patterns. Its lightweight and sheer texture give it a grace and elegance of its own. This fabric is suitable for sarees, suits, dupattas, kurtas, dresses and stoles.

product_title: Blue - Hakoba Hand Block Ajrakh Print Natural Dyed Cotton Fabric 102
product_description:
Blue hakoba cutwork embroidered ajrakh fabric is crafted using natural-dyeing and resist block-printing techniques. This ancient craft is estimated to be around 4,500 years old. The Ajrakh artisans in India originally migrated from Sindh to the Kutch region of Gujarat and to Barmer in Rajasthan. Ajrakh is also the traditional attire of the Maldhari pastoral community of Bhuj. The process is long and detailed, involving multiple stages where each layer of colour is printed only after a resting period, allowing the cloth to absorb the dye fully. Made from pure cotton, it is ideal for creating kurtas, shirts, dresses or even home decor items.
A Note on Handmade Beauty
Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage, and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature, because no two pieces are ever alike.

product_title: Blue - Mothra Leheriya Tie-Dye Chanderi Silk Fabric 17
product_description: Blue leheriya tie-dye mothra fabric, crafted by master artisan Adil Hussain, follows a centuries-old tradition from Rajasthan. In this technique, the fabric is folded and tied twice in opposite diagonals, creating a fine crisscross pattern with small square dots or a net like effect between the stripes. ‘Mothra’ refers to a pattern resembling tiny lentil grains. Made from a blend of chanderi silk and mercerised cotton, it has a light feel with a slight sheen. Each piece turns out slightly different due to the process. It can be used for sarees, dupattas, kurta sets, dress materials, as well as decor accents like curtains or soft furnishings.

After dyeing, the resist is washed away to reveal distinct patterns. Each piece reflects the skill, experience and careful craftsmanship of trained artisans. This fabric is suitable for sarees, suits, dupattas, kurtas, dresses and home decor items.

Each piece is hand block printed and dyed using natural colors over a slow process of 15–20 days. As a result, you may notice slight variations in color, mild pigment smudges or irregular dye patterns, these are not defects. They’re gentle marks of authenticity, proudly bearing the touch of human hands, heritage, and nature’s own palette. Wear them like a signature, because no two pieces are ever alike.

The process is long and intricate, involving multiple stages where each layer of colour is printed only after a resting period, allowing the fabric to fully absorb the dye. Its light, airy texture and sheer quality give it an elegant and graceful appeal, making it suitable for clothing like sarees, dupattas and kurtas, as well as decor uses.
Note: This piece carries tiny knots, thread pulls or uneven lines not flaws but traces of the limited handmade work involved in its making. Every irregularity reflects the human touch behind the process. It’s what happens when tradition passes through skilled hands. If you’re looking for absolute perfection, this may not be it. But if you appreciate character and authenticity, you’ve found it.
